# Monthly Household Budget Visualization Plan

Income is **$6,200/month**. Total listed expenses are **$5,415**, leaving **$785** unallocated before any extra buffer or discretionary spending.
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-dollar.svg

## Bar Chart and Pie Chart Grouping Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bar-chart.svg

### Bar chart plan
Use a **category-by-category bar chart** to compare monthly spending amounts.

- X-axis: category
- Y-axis: USD spent
- Sort bars: highest to lowest for quick concentration reading
- Highlight **Savings** in a different color so it is visually separated from spending
- Add a reference line for **monthly income = $6,200**

Recommended bars:
- Rent — **$1,900**
- Childcare — **$700**
- Groceries — **$620**
- Dining out — **$340**
- Miscellaneous — **$310**
- Insurance — **$260**
- Transport — **$210**
- Utilities — **$180**
- Subscriptions — **$95**
- Savings — **$800**

### Pie chart plan
Use a **grouped pie chart** so the chart stays readable instead of slicing into too many tiny pieces.

Suggested groups:
- **Housing** = Rent = **$1,900**
- **Family & essentials** = Groceries + Childcare + Insurance + Utilities + Transport = **$1,970**
- **Lifestyle** = Dining out + Subscriptions + Miscellaneous = **$745**
- **Savings** = **$800**

This grouping makes the chart easier to read and shows where money is going at a higher level.

## Spending Concentration and Savings Opportunities
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/pie-chart.svg

| Group | Categories Included | Monthly Total | Share of Income |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Housing | Rent | $1,900 | 30.6% |
| Family & essentials | Groceries, Childcare, Insurance, Utilities, Transport | $1,970 | 31.8% |
| Lifestyle | Dining out, Subscriptions, Miscellaneous | $745 | 12.0% |
| Savings | Savings | $800 | 12.9% |
| Unallocated income | Income minus listed items | $785 | 12.7% |

### 4 insights
- **Housing is the largest single cost** at **30.6% of income**. If rent can be reduced even modestly, the impact on monthly flexibility is large.
- **Family & essentials absorb the biggest combined share** at **31.8%**, driven mainly by childcare and groceries. These are likely necessary costs, so optimization here should focus on efficiency, not cuts.
- **Lifestyle spending is relatively contained** at **12.0%**, but it still offers the easiest savings opportunity because dining out and subscriptions are the most flexible categories.
- **Savings is strong at $800/month**, but total spending still leaves **$785 unallocated**. That amount could be redirected to emergency savings, debt payoff, or a sinking fund.

## Best Chart for 6-Month Change Tracking
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/graph-up.svg

For **month-to-month change over 6 months**, the best choice is a **multi-line chart**.

Why it works best:
- Shows trends clearly across time
- Makes it easy to compare categories like **rent, groceries, dining out, savings**
- Reveals seasonality, spikes, and gradual drift
- Works better than a bar chart when the goal is change over time rather than one-month composition

Best lines to track:
- Total spending
- Savings
- Housing
- Essentials
- Lifestyle spending
